solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Like garage door, maybe — done twice

parts.note: done in the sense of finished, as in 'time is up'
twice asks for a second word for done: over, as in 'the game is over'

explanation.surface: A puzzled description of a garage door that seems to have been finished off twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'twice' is not a doubling of one word: it asks for two different words that each mean 'done', UP and OVER.
explanation.definitionFit: An up-and-over garage door swings upward and over on its hinges, so the term describes that style of door.

clue.text: Clown about, lifting hearts with French horn and pipe music

indicators.note: about signals turning the clown's name round so it reads the other way

parts.note: Bip was the clown character played by the mime Marcel Marceau

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting means the pieces are raised so they read from the bottom up

parts.note: H is the card-suit abbreviation for hearts
cor is the French word for horn

explanation.surface: A clown fooling around, cheering everyone up with a French horn and some bagpipe tunes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns BIP into PIB; 'lifting' raises H and COR together so they read ROCH.
explanation.definitionFit: A pibroch is the classical music of the Scottish Highland bagpipe, a piece of theme and variations.

clue.text: Two goes at curling don't get used

indicators.note: curling bends the words round, rearranging the letters of the three words

explanation.surface: Two turns at the winter sport of curling that end up never being played.
explanation.walkthrough: Curling, the ice sport with stones, is the anagram signal on TWO GOES AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that go to waste are left unused and lost, an idiom for not being put to use.

clue.text: Possibly remote stronghold put in broadcast

indicators.note: broadcast means put out on air, so the words are heard rather than read

parts.note: a keep is the strongest tower of a castle; to pad is to put in filler, as when padding out a text

explanation.surface: A distant fortress being placed inside something sent out over the airwaves.
explanation.walkthrough: KEEP PAD said aloud runs together as KEY-PAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A TV remote control is one example of a keypad, a small panel of buttons, hence 'possibly'.

clue.text: Sleeps off very good brewery wares, not one English

parts.note: so good, i.e. very good: so is an intensifier

indicators.note: not one says a single letter is dropped from the beers, leaving one of the pair

parts.note: the products of a brewery are beers

explanation.surface: Someone sleeping off an excellent night of the brewery's products.
explanation.walkthrough: SO is read off 'very good' as in 'so good'. BEERS loses one of its two Es. Garfield Sobers is the theme: he hit six sixes in an over off Malcolm Nash of Glamorgan in 1968.
explanation.definitionFit: To sober up after drinking is to sleep off the effects of alcohol, so sobers works as a verb here.

clue.text: Queen's changing church order

indicators.note: changing means the letters of the word are altered in order

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: The Queen altering the way things are done in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'order' reads as a church decree but is the definition; 'changing' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A sequence is an order of succession, the way one item follows another.

clue.text: Canalman noisily deep-fried appetiser?

indicators.note: noisily says the word must be heard spoken, not read

parts.note: a bargee is a man who works a canal barge

explanation.surface: A canal boatman loudly ordering a fried Indian starter.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British accent, with the R silent, BARGEE is pronounced like BHAJI.
explanation.definitionFit: An onion bhaji is a spiced fritter fried in hot oil and served as a starter in Indian restaurants.

clue.text: Security of Tier F smoke screens? No

indicators.note: to screen is to shield or hide, so the smoke surrounds the letter

parts.note: reek is a Scottish and northern word for smoke
not, as in 'not at all'

explanation.surface: Asking whether smoke screens protect a certain tier of something.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'tier' here is one who ties; 'Tier F' looks like a single label, but the def ends at Tier and F is a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A reef knot is a secure square knot, the reliable fastening a person tying a rope would trust.

clue.text: See 17
About to infiltrate working party, even now

indicators.note: to infiltrate is to get inside, so the about word goes into the party

parts.note: a squad is a group working together
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A spy slipping into a working group to report back, even at this moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'even now' means 'level at this point', as with debts or scores now square.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounts that are squared are settled and level, so the word means even at present.

clue.text: Things that begin rankling Glamorgan's outfielders? 12 is first sign …

indicators.note: is first means the six comes before the other letters

parts.note: 12 refers to the answer at 12-down, six, which is VI in Roman numerals

indicators.note: the things that begin each word are its opening letters

explanation.surface: Part of a running account of the famous over: Glamorgan's fielders smarting as the first six goes up.
explanation.walkthrough: The clues from here to 26 run on with dots, telling the story of Sobers' six sixes off Glamorgan; each answer is a 'six' of some kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Virgo is the sixth sign of the zodiac, one of the twelve astrological star signs.

clue.text: Stars not the first to blow chances

indicators.note: not the first says the opening letter is dropped

parts.note: to blow money is to waste it
risks are chances taken

explanation.surface: Celebrities who fail to make the most of their opportunities.
explanation.walkthrough: WASTE loses its W.
explanation.definitionFit: Asterisks are star-shaped printed marks, and the word itself comes from Greek for little star.

clue.text: See 19
No good slipping up, wanting to do in king

indicators.note: in places the cleaning word inside the remainder
slipping means letters fall away from the word

parts.note: a jockey who is 'up' is riding the horse
to char is to do cleaning work

explanation.surface: A villain stumbling over a plot to murder the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: A jockey 'up' on a horse is riding it. 'slipping' drops N and G from RIDING to leave RIDI, and 'in' puts the cleaning word inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard I, known as the Lionheart, was the English king who reigned from 1189 to 1199.

clue.text: … over goes number two, not quite an exact copy …

indicators.note: over goes means the combined letters are turned to run backwards
not quite says the last letter is missing

parts.note: a brace is a pair, two of something

explanation.surface: The second six of the over goes up, and it's nearly a replica of the first.
explanation.walkthrough: BRACE loses its E to give BRAC; NO BRAC read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A carbon, short for carbon copy, is a duplicate made with carbon paper; carbon is also element number six.

clue.text: In harsh lesson it may be torn when taking excursion on holiday

definitions.text: In harsh lesson it may be torn

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a trip is an outing
someone off work is on holiday

explanation.surface: Something ripped while a person heads out on a trip during their holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tear a strip off' someone is a British idiom for a severe telling-off.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom to tear a strip off means to scold harshly, so the phrase is the thing torn in a rebuke.

clue.text: Disease caused by deficiency in an area around neck wound

indicators.note: around puts the first pieces outside the reversed word

parts.note: per means an, as in 'fifty pence an hour'

indicators.note: wound means wound round, so the word is turned back to front

parts.note: neck and gall both mean cheek or nerve

explanation.surface: A medical note on a deficiency disease affecting a wound on the neck.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neck' here is cheek or nerve, not the body part; 'wound' (pronounced like wind) reverses GALL to LLAG.
explanation.definitionFit: Pellagra is a disease brought on by a lack of niacin in the diet, causing dermatitis and diarrhoea.

clue.text: … show, in shot three, spin is taken on …

indicators.note: in places the spin and the two small words inside the scrambled number
shot means wrecked or broken, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: PR, public relations, is spin

explanation.surface: The commentary continues: in the third six, the ball's spin is met head on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' (ruined) rearranges THREE into THEER, with PRISON split in after the first three letters.
explanation.definitionFit: The Prisoner was a 1960s British TV series whose hero is known only as Number Six.

clue.text: What Goliath should know about David's grief?

parts.note: David's is read as David has
Goliath was felled by a stone from David's sling

explanation.surface: A wry question on what the giant ought to learn about the shepherd boy's sorrow.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of David's is 'has', not a possessive.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving someone grief means pestering them, which is just what hassling is.

clue.text: … the fourth to be deposited over front of square is returned by scorers …

indicators.note: over places the pieces before the next ones in the across entry
the fourth names a king's Roman numeral, as in George the Fourth, and that numeral is what gets deposed from the word
deposited means dethroned or removed, so the king's number leaves the word

parts.note: to live is to be, to exist
IV is the fourth in Roman numerals

indicators.note: front of picks the opening letter
returned says the little word is turned round

parts.note: X means by, as in 3 x 2 feet

explanation.surface: The fourth six lands over square leg and is thrown back by the scorers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deposited' is read as deposed: the king's numeral loses its throne in the word for 'to be'. 'by' is the multiplication sign, as in 3 by 2.
explanation.definitionFit: Les Six were a group of six French composers, so scorers in the sense of writers of musical scores.

clue.text: … gift for one backpedalling? Again, see ball ultimately transported over boundary's edge …

indicators.note: backpedalling is going backwards, so the abbreviation is reversed

parts.note: e.g., for example, is for one

indicators.note: transported means carried away, so these letters are rearranged
ultimately picks the closing letter
edge here is the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: The fifth six: the ball, ultimately, is carried over the boundary edge again.
explanation.walkthrough: EG reversed gives GE; 'transported' mixes AGAIN, SEE, L and Y into ESEALAYING.
explanation.definitionFit: Six geese a-laying is the sixth day's gift in the carol The Twelve Days of Christmas.

clue.text: Individual birthday tips?

indicators.note: tips means tips over, so the abbreviation is turned upside down

parts.note: DOB is date of birth

explanation.surface: A single person asking for advice on what to do for a birthday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tips' looks like advice; it means tips over, reversing DOB.
explanation.definitionFit: Bod is British slang for a person, a single body or fellow.

clue.text: See 26
Anagram solver with a line in workwear

indicators.note: in places the two pieces inside the scrambled word
the clue states outright that the word solver is rearranged

explanation.surface: A crossword solver at an anagram, dressed in a boiler suit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Anagram' is the indicator itself; it makes OVERLS, which the A and L split.
explanation.definitionFit: Overalls are protective garments worn over clothes for manual work.

clue.text: Virgin loves talking (full of it)

indicators.note: full of it says the answer sits within these words

explanation.surface: A chaste person who adores chatting, and is full of themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A vestal is a chaste woman, from the Vestal Virgins who tended the sacred fire of Vesta in Rome.

clue.text: Drink shot with charges

indicators.note: charges means loads, so the shot is filled with the other word

parts.note: a shy is a throw, a shot at something, as at a coconut shy
and means with, joining things

explanation.surface: A drink fired off together with some accusations.
explanation.definitionFit: A shandy is beer mixed with lemonade, a light drink popular in British pubs.

clue.text: … player, having dispersed disheartened keeper and infield, belted Nash out of the ground

indicators.note: dispersed means scattered, so the whole pool of letters is rearranged after the three are removed
disheartened removes the middle of the word, leaving its ends

explanation.surface: The final six: Sobers scattering the keeper and fielders, belting Nash out of the ground.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of the' takes T, H, E out of KR INFIELD BELTED NASH, and the rest is rearranged. Malcolm Nash was the Glamorgan bowler who conceded the six sixes in 1968.
explanation.definitionFit: In rugby union the blindside flanker wears the number six shirt, a forward who plays on the narrow side.

clue.text: Woman on a meandering route out of London

indicators.note: meandering means wandering about, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the M1 is the motorway from London to the north of England, its 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: A woman taking a winding road away from the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'meandering' looks like a description of the route; it rearranges ON A.
explanation.definitionFit: Naomi is a woman's name, borne by the mother-in-law of Ruth in the Bible.

clue.text: Image of group seeking to preserve secretary's make-up?

definitions.text: Image of group seeking to preserve

parts.note: a secretary is a PA, and the clue's words describe what PA is made up of, its two letters with 'and' between them

explanation.surface: A picture of an office group trying to keep a secretary's cosmetics safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make-up' is not cosmetics but composition: PA is made of P and A.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant panda is the logo of the WWF, the conservation charity working to protect wildlife.

clue.text: Inability to recognise one heir when back within range

indicators.note: within puts the reversed pieces inside the cooker

parts.note: an Aga is a British brand of range cooker

indicators.note: when back says the pieces are read backwards

parts.note: I is one, the Roman numeral
a son is a male heir

explanation.surface: Failing to spot a returning heir among a group of hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' looks like mountains; it is an Aga, a heavy British cooking stove. I SON backwards gives NOSI.
explanation.definitionFit: Agnosia is a medical term for losing the ability to identify objects, faces or sounds.

clue.text: President's kinky life as dame, retrospectively?

indicators.note: life as a dame is life in women's dress, so the life word goes in the dress word
looking back, the dress word is read in reverse

parts.note: a pantomime dame is a man in drag

indicators.note: kinky means twisted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A president's bizarre secret life dressed as a pantomime dame, looked back on.
explanation.walkthrough: A pantomime dame is a British Christmas show role played by a man in drag; 'retrospectively' makes GARD and 'kinky' makes FIEL.
explanation.definitionFit: James Garfield was the 20th US President; Garfield Sobers is the cricketer of the theme.
